theory.intro: A **net** is a flat pattern of polygons that folds up to make a 3-D object. The polygons in the net are the **faces** of the solid.
facts: A net of a **cube** is $6$ squares (e.g. a cross or T shape).
A net of a **rectangular prism** is $6$ rectangles.
A net of a **square pyramid** is $1$ square with a triangle on each of its $4$ sides.
A net of a **triangular prism** is $2$ triangles and $3$ rectangles.
steps: Count how many polygons there are and name each shape.
Two matching polygons + rectangles → a prism; one polygon + triangles → a pyramid.
Name the solid after that base shape.

foundation.solution_text: The net has six equal square faces and folds to a cube.
The two triangles are matching bases and the three rectangles join them, so it is a triangular prism.
The square is the base and the four triangles meet at an apex, so it is a square pyramid.
No. The $2\times3$ rectangle makes faces overlap when folded and cannot close a cube.

foundation.question_text: List the faces needed in a net for a rectangular prism.
foundation.solution_text: A rectangular prism needs six rectangular faces arranged as three matching pairs.

foundation.question_text: List the faces needed in a net for a triangular pyramid.
foundation.solution_text: A triangular pyramid needs four triangular faces.

development.solution_text: It folds to a rectangular prism, and its bases are rectangles.
With two triangular bases and three rectangular side faces, it becomes a triangular prism.

development.question_text: A net contains two pentagons and five rectangles. Name the solid and explain the role of the pentagons.
development.solution_text: It is a pentagonal prism; the pentagons are its two identical bases.

development.question_text: A net contains one hexagon and six triangles. Name the solid.
development.solution_text: It is a hexagonal pyramid because the hexagon is the base and the triangles meet at an apex.
Each triangle is attached to one side of the square, so their free vertices come together to form the apex.
Add one square joined to the base edge of each triangle arrangement so the four triangles surround it.

mastery.question_text: A net has $2$ congruent hexagons and $6$ rectangles. Predict its number of faces and name the solid.
mastery.solution_text: It has $2+6=8$ faces and folds to a hexagonal prism.

mastery.question_text: A student draws one pentagon with only four triangles around it and calls it a pentagonal-pyramid net. Diagnose the error.
mastery.solution_text: A pentagon has five sides, so it needs five triangular side faces. One triangle is missing.

mastery.question_text: Two cube nets each use six squares but have different layouts. Explain why both can be correct.
mastery.solution_text: A net is valid if its squares fold onto the six different faces without overlap; more than one flat arrangement can do this.
